normalized.subject: very massive stars
normalized.relation_definition: The stellar class or evolutionary state that a specified type of massive star transitions into at the end of its lifecycle.
normalized.direction: type of massive star -> terminal stellar class
normalized.canonical_fact: Very massive stars end their lives by becoming red supergiants.
normalized.prompt_en: How do very massive stars end their lives?
evidence_quotes: How do very massive stars end their lives?
normalized.reason: Source explicitly states very massive stars end their lives by becoming red supergiants. No existing catalog relation captures a terminal evolutionary-state transition (entity_to_class implies stable membership, not a lifecycle endpoint). Proposed new relation 'stellar_object_to_terminal_stellar_class' to precisely encode the direction 'massive-star type → terminal stellar class'.

normalized.subject: citrate
normalized.relation_definition: The parent molecular compound from which a specified ionized or derived chemical species originates through proton transfer.
normalized.direction: ion/derived chemical form -> parent molecular compound
normalized.canonical_fact: Citrate is an ionized form of citric acid.
normalized.prompt_en: What compound is citrate an ionized form of?
evidence_quotes: What is citrate an ionized form of?
normalized.reason: Source explicitly states citrate is an ionized form of citric acid. No existing catalog relation captures an ion-to-parent-compound chemical relationship (entity_to_class is taxonomy-level; entity_to_material is composition; abbreviation_to_expansion is naming). Proposed new relation 'chemical_species_to_parent_molecule' to precisely encode 'ionized form → parent molecular compound via proton transfer'.
